summary:
La Roja is an Argentine province and stands under the national framework in full: legal gender change under Law 26.743, the X marker on national identity documents under Decree 476/2021, and the rules on care for minors that a federal court struck down in April 2025. That layer is carried by Argentina's national record; the findings here are those specific to La Roja.

No provincial reporting infrastructure generates trans-specific records for La Roja. The only systematic count covering the province is the national hate-crime observatory, which does not disaggregate its 2025 total by province or by victim group, so no published figure describes La Roja on its own.

Reporting from April 2025 records that police violence against trans and travesti sex workers has worsened since the change of national government and is worst outside Buenos Aires, in the interior provinces. La Roja is not named in that reporting. The claim describes a regional pattern that includes the province rather than a documented provincial incident, and no provincial source corroborates or quantifies it.

A visitor or resident in La Roja therefore meets the national legal protections without a provincial layer of enforcement data behind them: there is no provincial tally of hate-crime investigations, no provincial record of police conduct toward trans people, and no local body publishing either.
tangentialFactors:
Local anti-discrimination coverage in Argentina is recorded only for Buenos Aires city and Rosario. No provincial or municipal ordinance covering gender identity or expression is recorded for La Roja, so a complaint arising in the province has no local statutory route of the kind those two cities provide.

The national anti-discrimination agency was abolished and shut down in February 2024. With no provincial body recorded for La Roja, a discrimination complaint originating in the province has neither a local authority nor the former national agency to receive it.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of La Roja appear in the national hate-crime count without provincial attribution, because the observatory that compiles it publishes no breakdown by province. A report made in the province enters a national total and cannot be traced back to La Roja in any published data.

The provincial police are the force implicated by the interior-province account of worsening violence against trans and travesti sex workers, and no provincial review, inspectorate finding or disciplinary record addressing that conduct is cited in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether La Roja has any provincial or municipal provision covering discrimination on grounds of gender identity is unresolved in the sources; the local coverage recorded nationally is limited to Buenos Aires city and Rosario.

The April 2025 account of police violence worsening in the interior provinces does not name La Roja, and no provincial incident, case or investigation is documented for the province. The national observatory's 2025 total is a raw count aggregating sexual orientation and gender identity, with no population denominator and no provincial disaggregation, and cannot be read as a rate for La Roja.
